answer: Each new agent locks a refundable bond in a delayed-unlock queue called the willow, which releases only after a peer panel finalizes its checks. A published VRF seed samples K established graders; each independently recomputes the applicant's last N attested nonces against ledger timestamps and signs an edge, and those edges form a trellis any peer can replay from public data. When a tide of fresh addresses shares inter-arrival gaps or one parent payout, the panel cites those traces, slashes the common bond in the willow, and voids the seats.
